science.claim: If the sun stops moving across the sky, the Earth has stopped spinning.
science.working: The sun's daily path across the sky is caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis (one turn per sidereal day, 23 h 56 min 4 s), not by the sun moving around us. For the sun to stand still in the sky, the rotation must stop.
science.source: Basic astronomy: diurnal motion (e.g. NASA Space Place, 'Why do we have day and night?')

science.claim: Anywhere in Indonesia, you are moving at more than 1,600 km/h with the Earth's spin, and you would keep that speed if the Earth stopped.
science.working: Equatorial circumference 2 x pi x 6,378.137 km = 40,075 km; one rotation takes 23.934 h, so the equator moves 40,075 / 23.934 = 1,674 km/h (465 m/s). At latitude L the speed is 1,674 x cos(L). Indonesia spans about 6 N (Sabang, 5.9 N) to 11 S (Pulau Ndana, 11.0 S): the slowest point is 1,674 x cos(11 deg) = 1,643 km/h; Jakarta (6.2 S) is 1,664 km/h. So 'more than 1,600 km/h' holds everywhere in Indonesia. By inertia (Newton's first law) anything not fixed to the bedrock, the air included, keeps moving east at that speed if the ground stops.
science.source: WGS 84 equatorial radius 6,378.137 km; IERS sidereal day 86,164.1 s; Newton's first law; geography of Indonesia (Sabang 5.9 N, Pulau Ndana 11.0 S)
